newsitem.title: JORDAN: Mideast violence hits Amman stocks at week's start.
newsitem.headline: Mideast violence hits Amman stocks at week's start.

text.p: Israeli-Palestinian violence kept Jordanian stocks pinned down at the start of weekly trade on Saturday in spite of a number of strong individual performances, dealers said.

The Amman Financial Market 60-share index dropped 0.86 percent to 148.30 points from 149.59 points on Wednesday, the last day of weekly trading. A total of 465,680 shares changed hands for 640,401 dinars ($913) million.
"As if the market, which was already calming down after a recent rebound, needed an excuse to weaken," said one dealer. "And this excuse was provided by the violence..." he added.

After gradual gains earlier this month that sent the market back above 150 points last week for the first time in four months, shares ran out of steam in mid-week with stock moving lower in thin volume.
The market has long been sensitive to any Middle East development, whether good or bad.
Industrials continued to dominate trade on Saturday.

Market leader Arab Bank, which propelled the index upwards in the first half of September, appeared to lack impetus with none of the large volume witnessed recently. Its stock, the most expensive on the Amman exchange, fell to 242 dinars from 245.500 dinars in low trade.
Brokers fear the market may be running out of steam as institutional investors continue to wait in the sidelines and stocks run into profit-taking after the bourse's recent results-driven rally.

Star performer Livestock and Poultry, which has been a focus of investor interest for the fourth week in a row, remainched unchanged at 0.90 dinars but was among the few blue chips dominating trade with a 277,368 dinar turnover.
Dealers say shareholders realising profit on their holdings are feeding the persistent speculative trade on the stock that has seen no fundamentals emerging to otherwise attract investors.
The Middle East Investment Bank fell 1.09 dinars from 1.15 dinars.
Jordan Phosphate Mines Company, lost 0.05 fils from 3.25 dinars with 200 shares changing hands.
Of 35 stocks traded, 25 fell and three were unchanged.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange fell 0.56 percent to 82.13 points, still 14.01 percent down from the same time last year.
